titulo: Wish, if only, would rather, it's time
titulo_es: Wish, if only, would rather, it's time (wishes, regrets and preferences)
descripcion_es: Expressing unreal wishes and regrets with wish/if only; preferences with would rather; it's (high) time.
resumen: After wish, if only, would rather (+ another person) and it's time we use a tense shifted “back”: the past for the present and the past perfect for the past. Wish + would expresses a complaint or a wish for someone to change.

filas: I wish I had more time. (es: ojalá tuviera)
I wish I hadn't said that. (es: ojalá no hubiera dicho)
ability you would like to have
complaint: I want someone else to change
I wish you would stop shouting.
preference about what someone else does
I'd rather you didn't smoke here.
it should already have been done

explicacion.texto: With be, were can be used for all persons, especially in careful speech and writing: I wish I were taller. If only he were here.
We do not say I wish I would: for yourself, use could or the past. For wishes about the future that can come true, we do not use wish but hope: I hope you pass (es: espero que apruebes).

items: If only is more emphatic than wish: If only I had listened!
Would rather + infinitive without to, and than to compare: I'd rather walk than take the bus.
It's time + to + infinitive is also possible: It's time to go.

ejemplos.frase: I wish I lived closer to the sea.
ejemplos.traduccion: Ojalá viviera más cerca del mar.

ejemplos.frase: If only we had bought that flat ten years ago!
ejemplos.traduccion: ¡Ojalá hubiéramos comprado ese piso hace diez años!

ejemplos.frase: I wish my neighbours would turn the music down.
ejemplos.traduccion: Ojalá mis vecinos bajaran la música.

ejemplos.frase: I'd rather you didn't tell anyone about this.
ejemplos.traduccion: Preferiría que no se lo contaras a nadie.

ejemplos.frase: It's high time the government did something about housing.
ejemplos.traduccion: Ya es hora de que el Gobierno haga algo con la vivienda.

ejemplos.frase: She wishes she could speak Japanese.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I wish I have a car.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I wish I had a car.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Wish about the present takes the past simple.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I wish you pass your exams.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I hope you pass your exams.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: For possible wishes use hope, not wish.
It's time + subject takes the past even when it refers to the present.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: I wish I ___ (know) the answer, but I don't.
ejercicios.explicacion: The first row of the table applies: wish + past simple for a wish about the present. The clue is “but I don't”: at this moment he does not know the answer. The verb moves back one tense, from know to knew, even though the situation is current; it is equivalent to the Spanish imperfect subjunctive “supiera”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Wish about the present: past simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ojalá supiera la respuesta, pero no la sé.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After wish the present moves back to the past: knew.
The past perfect would be for the past (“I wish I had known”); here the situation is present.
With the same subject (I wish I…) would is not used; for the present use the past simple.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: If only I ___ (not / eat) so much at dinner last night!
ejercicios.explicacion: The row for wish / if only + past perfect applies, for regrets about the past. The clue is “last night”: the action has already happened and cannot be changed. The verb goes in the negative past perfect: hadn't eaten (had not eaten). If only is more emphatic than wish.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Regret about the past: past perfect.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The past simple after if only would express a wish about the present; for something that happened last night you need the past perfect.
The past participle of eat is eaten, not ate.
Would cannot be used to regret something you yourself have already done.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: I'd rather you ___ (come) tomorrow instead of today.
ejercicios.explicacion: The row for would rather + person + past applies, for preferences about what someone else does. The clue is that another person, you, appears after I'd rather. So the verb goes in the past simple, came, even though we are talking about the future (tomorrow). If it were your own preference, it would take the infinitive without to.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Would rather + another person + past simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: Preferiría que vinieras mañana en lugar de hoy.

errores_previstos.explicacion: With another person after would rather the verb goes in the past, came; the infinitive is only for your own preference.
Would rather never takes to.
Even though we are talking about tomorrow, would rather + person takes the past simple.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: It's about time you ___ (start) looking for a job.
ejercicios.explicacion: The row for it's (about) time + subject + past applies: it shows that something should already be happening. The clue is “It's about time you…”: there is a subject after time. That is why the verb goes in the past, started, even though it refers to the present or the immediate future.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ya va siendo hora de que empieces a buscar trabajo.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After it's time + subject the verb goes in the past, not the present.
It's time to start exists, but without a subject; with you before it, you need the past.
The past perfect is not used with it's time; the past simple is enough.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of be.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card points out that, with be, were can be used after wish for all persons, especially in careful language, and was in speech. The clue is “already”: the speaker wishes the present were different. So both answers are accepted: were, more formal, and was, more informal.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Past of be after wish; were is more formal.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After wish the present moves back to the past: were or was.
Wish + would is kept for complaints about other people's actions, not for states such as the weather.
The past perfect would be a regret about the past; here it is a wish about the present.

ejercicios.frase: I wish you ___ leaving your clothes on the floor.
ejercicios.explicacion: The row for wish + person + would applies; it expresses a complaint and the wish that another person changes their behaviour. The clue is leaving your clothes on the floor, an annoying habit of someone else (you). So: I wish you would stop. The other tenses do not convey that request for change.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Complaint about someone else's habit: wish + person + would.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ojalá dejaras de tirar la ropa al suelo.

por_opcion.would stop: Correct: wish + person + would to complain about someone else's habit and ask them to change.
por_opcion.stopped: Incorrect in this sense: the past describes a wish about a situation, not a complaint about behaviour; with stop + -ing it does not convey the request for change the sentence needs.
por_opcion.will stop: Incorrect: will is not used after wish; for possible wishes you would use hope.
por_opcion.had stopped: Incorrect: the past perfect would regret something in the past, and here the habit is still going on.

ejercicios.frase: I wish I ___ play the piano like you.
ejercicios.explicacion: The row for wish / if only + could applies, for an ability you would like to have. The clue is play the piano: it is about knowing how to do something. For the speakers themselves, the card warns that we never say I wish I would; we use could. Can does not work either, because after wish the tense moves back.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Ability you want for yourself: could (never I wish I would).
ejercicios.traduccion: Ojalá supiera tocar el piano como tú.

por_opcion.could: Correct: wish + could for a skill you would like to have.
por_opcion.would: Incorrect: I wish I would is not used; with the same subject we use could or the past.
por_opcion.can: Incorrect: after wish the present moves back; can becomes could.

ejercicios.frase: I'd rather ___ by train than fly.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that would rather + infinitive without to expresses your own preference, and that we compare with than. The clue is that there is no other person after I'd rather: it is the speaker who prefers. So: I'd rather travel by train than fly, with both verbs in the infinitive without to.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Would rather + infinitive without to for your own preference.
ejercicios.traduccion: Prefiero ir en tren a ir en avión.

por_opcion.travel: Correct: would rather + infinitive without to for your own preference.
por_opcion.to travel: Incorrect: would rather does not take to (would prefer does).
por_opcion.travelled: Incorrect: the past is only used when the preference refers to another person (I'd rather you travelled).
por_opcion.travelling: Incorrect: would rather does not go with -ing.

ejercicios.frase: Good luck tomorrow! I ___ the interview goes well.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card warns that for wishes about the future that can come true, we do not use wish but hope. The clue is “Good luck tomorrow!”: the interview has not happened yet and may go well. Hope is followed by a normal tense (goes), without moving back.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Possible wish about the future: hope.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¡Suerte mañana! Espero que la entrevista vaya bien.

por_opcion.hope: Correct: hope for possible wishes; it goes with normal tenses (I hope it goes well).
por_opcion.wish: Incorrect: wish expresses unreal wishes and would need a past; I wish the interview goes well is not correct.
por_opcion.would rather: Incorrect: would rather expresses a preference between options and would be followed by a past (I'd rather it went); it does not fit with goes.

ejercicios.frase: I wish I would be younger.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card says that I wish I would is not used: for a wish about yourself in the present, use the past. The clue is the repeated subject (I wish I…) and the state be younger. So: I wish I were younger, in careful language, or I wish I was younger, in speech; both are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: I wish I would is not used; use the past (were/was).

errores_previstos.respuesta: I wish I would be younger.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: with the same subject would is not used.
After wish the present moves back to the past: were or was.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I wish I had been younger.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past perfect regrets something in the past; being younger now is a wish about the present.

ejercicios.frase: She wishes she didn't sell her old guitar last year.
respuestas: She wishes she hadn't sold her old guitar last year.
She wishes she had not sold her old guitar last year.
ejercicios.explicacion: The row for wish + past perfect applies, for regrets about the past. The clue is “last year”: the sale has already happened. The mistake is using the past simple, which would be a wish about the present. The correction is hadn't sold (had not sold), with the irregular past participle of sell.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Regret about the past (last year): past perfect.
ejercicios.traduccion: Le gustaría no haber vendido su vieja guitarra el año pasado.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She wishes she didn't sell her old guitar last year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: for the past you need the past perfect.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She wishes she hadn't sell her old guitar last year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After hadn't comes the past participle, sold.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She wishes she wouldn't have sold her old guitar last year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Wish + would have is not the normal form for regretting something you did; use the past perfect.

ejercicios.frase: It's high time we go to bed.
respuestas: It's high time we went to bed.
It is high time we went to bed.
ejercicios.explicacion: The row for it's (high) time + subject + past applies. The clue is we after high time: there is a subject, so the verb goes in the past, went, even though the action is immediate. High time adds the nuance that we should already have done it. The uncontracted form It is is also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: It's high time + subject + past simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ya es hora de que nos acostemos.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It's high time we go to bed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: after it's time + subject comes the past.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It's high time we will go to bed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Will is not used here; the verb goes in the past simple.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It's high time we had gone to bed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past perfect is not used with it's time; went is enough.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence starting with I wish.
ejercicios.frase: I'm sorry I didn't call my grandmother more often.
respuestas: I wish I had called my grandmother more often.
I wish I'd called my grandmother more often.
ejercicios.explicacion: The row for wish + past perfect applies: regret for something that was not done in the past. The clue is “I'm sorry I didn't call”: the regret is about the past. When you change to I wish, the negative becomes affirmative (what you wish is that you had called) and the verb goes in the past perfect: had called, or the contraction I'd called.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Regret about the past: wish + past perfect.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ojalá hubiera llamado a mi abuela más a menudo.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I wish I called my grandmother more often.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past simple would express a wish about the present; the regret is about the past.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I wish I hadn't called my grandmother more often.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The negative is kept, but the meaning changes: it would say you regret having called her.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I wish I would have called my grandmother more often.
errores_previstos.explicacion: You hear it in speech, but the standard form is wish + past perfect, without would have.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence with I'd rather.
ejercicios.frase: Please don't park your car in front of my garage.
respuestas: I'd rather you didn't park your car in front of my garage.
I would rather you didn't park your car in front of my garage.
I'd rather you did not park your car in front of my garage.
I would rather you did not park your car in front of my garage.
ejercicios.explicacion: The row for would rather + person + past applies, which the card presents as a polite way of asking for something. The clue is that the request is addressed to another person. So: I'd rather you didn't park, with the negative past even though it refers to the present or future. Contracted and uncontracted forms are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Polite request: would rather + person + past.
ejercicios.traduccion: Preferiría que no aparcaras el coche delante de mi garaje.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'd rather you don't park your car in front of my garage.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With another person after would rather, the verb goes in the past: didn't park.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'd rather you not to park your car in front of my garage.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Would rather + person is not built with to; it takes a clause in the past.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'd rather that you don't park your car in front of my garage.
errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish “que” with the present; you need the past (didn't park).

ejercicios.explicacion: The card says that if only + past perfect expresses an emphatic regret about the past. The order is if only, the subject I and the past perfect had listened. If only works as a fixed block and always goes at the beginning, like Spanish “ojalá”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: If only + past perfect for an emphatic regret.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Only if means “only on condition that”; the regret is if only.
After if only the subject is not inverted; it is I had listened.

glosario.definicion_l: hear with intention · listen and pay attention

ejercicios.explicacion: The card gives it's time + subject + past. The order is it's time, the subject we and the verb in the past, left. Although the action is immediate, the verb goes in the past because it is presented as something that should already be happening.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ya es hora de que nos vayamos.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject we goes before the verb left.
The expression it's time goes at the beginning and the clause with a subject comes after.

descripcion_larga_es: Wish and if only express unreal wishes and regrets (Spanish “ojalá tuviera”, “ojalá no hubiera dicho”); would rather expresses preferences, and it's time says that something should already be done. They all use a tense shifted back: the past for the present and the past perfect for the past. It is hard for Spanish speakers because where Spanish uses the subjunctive English uses the past, and because “ojalá apruebes” is not wish but hope.

contexto.que_es: These are structures for talking about unreal or unwanted situations. Wish and if only go with the past simple (unreal present), the past perfect (unreal past) or could (ability you would like to have); wish + person + would expresses a complaint. Would rather goes with the infinitive without to for your own preference and with person + past for someone else's. It's (high/about) time + subject + past shows that something should already be happening.
contexto.por_que_importa: They let you express regret, polite complaints and nuanced preferences, which is highly valued at B2 level. Mixing up the tenses changes the meaning (I wish I knew versus I wish I had known), and using wish for possible wishes (“I wish you pass”) is a typical mistake an examiner spots immediately. I'd rather you didn't… is also a polite way of asking for something.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: To regret something present or past, complain about what someone else does, say what you prefer or point out that it is time to do something. The signals are Spanish “ojalá”, “me arrepiento”, “preferiría que”, “ya es hora de que”. Where Spanish uses the subjunctive (tuviera, hubiera, hicieras), English uses the past or past perfect; for wishes that can come true, hope.
